title: Quiet money catalog: low-profile billionaires/centimillionaires in data, surveillance, and political influence
source: Public record: SEC/ADV filings; FEC + IRS 990 (dark-money trusts); court records; investigative reporting (ProPublica, NYT, WSJ, OpenSecrets). Catalog layer (#208 batch 2). Structural overlay; person nodes carry Persons-tab dossiers. FOCUS: the deliberately quiet ultra-wealthy who shape data/surveillance infrastructure + politics from the shadows. HONESTY: donations/stakes/holdings are FACT (disclosed); influence + intent are graded; no coordinated-conspiracy imputed across independent actors.

edges.notes: Robert Mercer - former co-CEO of Renaissance Technologies (the Medallion quant fund; among the most successful + secretive hedge funds). A computer scientist (ex-IBM speech-recognition) whose quant fortune bankrolls political data-operations (fact).
The Mercers were the principal financial backers of Cambridge Analytica (~$15M+) - explicitly to build psychographic voter-targeting (fact).
Mercer money (with Bannon as intermediary) financed Breitbart News - the media/data/politics triad (fact).
Rebekah Mercer sat on Cambridge Analytica's board + drove its political deployment - the operational face of the family's data-politics project (fact).
Rebekah Mercer is a Breitbart part-owner/board member - and later co-founded Parler - extending the family's alt-media/data footprint (fact).

Cambridge Analytica harvested up to ~87M Facebook profiles (via a personality-quiz app) for psychographic targeting in 2016 - the scandal that exposed the social-data-to-political-manipulation pipeline; the firm collapsed (2018), FTC fined Facebook $5B (fact).

Cambridge Analytica combined harvested social data with commercial data-broker files to build individual psychographic profiles - the model that normalized political micro-targeting (fact); wires quiet money to the broker/surveillance thread.
Jeffrey Yass - co-founder of Susquehanna International Group (SIG), a giant options/quant trading firm; among the richest + lowest-profile Americans; a libertarian mega-donor (fact).

SIG holds a large early stake in ByteDance (TikTok's parent) - reportedly ~15%, making Yass a major indirect TikTok owner; central to the US TikTok-ban politics + his lobbying against it (fact of stake; influence graded).
Yass is a top funder of the Club for Growth (anti-tax) + a leading libertarian/GOP + school-choice donor - quiet but among the largest individual political givers (fact).
Yass/SIG are among the largest crypto-industry political donors (Fairshake super PAC ecosystem) - ties quiet money to the crypto-legislation thread (fact).

Barre Seid (electronics manufacturer, extremely private) gave his entire ~$1.6B company to the Marble Freedom Trust (2021) - the largest known political donation in US history, structured to avoid gift/estate tax (fact).
The Marble Freedom Trust is chaired/controlled by Leonard Leo - handing him a $1.6B war chest for conservative legal/political causes (fact).

Leonard Leo - the Federalist Society co-chair who built the judicial-nominee pipeline; not a billionaire himself but controls a multibillion-dollar dark-money network (Marble, the '85 Fund', etc.) - the quiet architect of the courts (fact).

The Federalist Society network shaped the selection of a supermajority of current Supreme Court justices - the institutionalized pipeline from movement to bench (fact of affiliation; 'control' framing graded).

Harlan Crow (Crow Holdings real estate; very low public profile) provided years of undisclosed luxury gifts/travel + a real-estate purchase to Justice Clarence Thomas - the documented judicial-ethics scandal (fact per ProPublica; characterization contested).
Crow is a longtime funder of conservative legal/policy institutions (AEI, Federalist-Society-adjacent) - the quiet-patron model (fact).

Timothy Mellon - reclusive Mellon banking-fortune heir (Guggenheim/rail); the single largest individual disclosed donor of the 2024 cycle (>$150M to a pro-Trump super PAC + tens of millions to RFK Jr's PAC), yet almost no public presence (fact of giving; motives opaque).

Hank Asher - the 'father of data fusion' (d. 2013). Founded Seisint, whose Accurint + the post-9/11 MATRIX database pioneered mass aggregation of public + commercial records for law enforcement - the origin of modern commercial mass-surveillance data-broking (fact).

Seisint built MATRIX (Multistate Anti-Terrorism Information Exchange, 2003) - a DHS/DOJ-funded cross-state person-search system; shut down 2005 after privacy backlash, but its approach became standard (fact).

LexisNexis (Reed Elsevier/RELX) acquired Seisint (2004, ~$775M) - folding Asher's data-fusion engine into what is now LexisNexis Risk Solutions, a core data broker across the auto/insurance/policing pipelines (fact).
Asher later founded TLO (TransUnion acquired it out of bankruptcy, 2014) - continuing the people-search/data-fusion model now embedded in TransUnion (fact).
TLO/TLOxp is a law-enforcement + private-investigator people-search product - a direct descendant of the Asher data-fusion lineage in the broker ecosystem (fact).
John Overdeck (with David Siegel) co-founded Two Sigma - a ~$60B+ quant/data-science hedge fund; both founders are low-profile centibillionaire-adjacent quants (fact).

Two Sigma is a pure data/ML-driven fund - part of the quiet quant-finance cluster (RenTech, Two Sigma, Citadel, DE Shaw) that pioneered industrial-scale data + AI before Big Tech; wires quiet money to the AI thread (fact of category).
